Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

proper adjective

real, complete, as it should be

also a proper meal, a proper job, regular (complete, full-scale), properly (fully)

classical

Caes. B.C. 1.23: iter jūstum, a regular day’s march (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 9.43: exercitus, an army at full strength (Lewis & Short)

jūstus, jūsta, jūstum

adjective, declension

proper, complete, regular, of the right size

Its first sense is just, righteous. Of things it means proper and complete: a full army, a regular battle, a wall of the proper height (Caes. B.G. 7.23) (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • rēctus, rēcta, rēctum — regular, formal (of a dinner)

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Suet. Dom. 7: rēctārum cēnārum cōnsuētūdō (Lewis & Short, s.v. regō); Mart. 2.69.7

    Cēna rēcta is a proper, formal dinner (Lewis & Short). Otherwise rēctus is straight, or right and correct (see correct).

Examples

  • rēctō ac jūstō proeliō dīmicāre

    to fight a proper, regular battleLiv. 35.4 (Lewis & Short, s.v. regō)

  • Hodiē rēctam cēnam nōn parāvī; pānis et cāseus satis erunt.

    I haven’t made a proper dinner today; bread and cheese will have to do.composed

See also appropriate, correct, real, regular.

SourcesLewis & Short: justus · Lewis & Short: rego

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
